issues.note: Plans and music are not put 'into order'; the core idea misdescribes senses 1 and 3.
The verb order does mean arrange in sequence (ordered by date); the synonym is valid.
The example is ungrammatical; arrange takes a to-infinitive, so the pattern label does not fit.
The 'put in order' sense never takes an -ing complement.
The slot item is acceptable; a concrete 'arrange something for piano' would be clearer.
The construction is named as a phrase, so double asterisks are correct house style.
Correct: it should read 'arranged to meet her'.

findings.F1: The core idea says plans and music are put 'into order', which misdescribes the planning and music senses.
findings.F2: The sense 1 example 'arranged meeting her' uses an -ing form; arrange takes a to-infinitive.
findings.F3: Sense 2 grammar lists a false 'verb + -ing form' pattern.
